<p id="mwDg"><b id="mwDw">Nintendo Classics</b><sup about="#mwt14" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"group":"lower-roman"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-3"},"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"efn-lr","href":"./Template:Efn-lr"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Formerly known only as \"Nintendo Switch Online classic game libraries\"; the service was rebranded as \"Nintendo Classics\" on April 2, 2025.&lt;ref>{{cite magazine | last=Kamen | first=Matt | title=How the GameCube Controller Works on Nintendo Switch 2—and How You Can Get One | magazine=WIRED | date=April 5, 2025 | url=https://www.wired.com/story/how-the-gamecube-controller-works-on-nintendo-switch-2-and-how-you-can-get-one/ | access-date=May 25, 2025 | archive-date=May 1, 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501103111/https://www.wired.com/story/how-the-gamecube-controller-works-on-nintendo-switch-2-and-how-you-can-get-one/ | url-status=live }}&lt;/ref>"}},"i":0}}]}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-3" data-mw-group="lower-roman" id="mwEA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEg">[</span>i<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEw">]</span></span></a></sup> is a line of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Video_game_console_emulator" title="Video game console emulator" id="mwFA">emulated</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Retro_games" title="Retro games" class="mw-redirect" id="mwFQ">retro games</a> distributed by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo" title="Nintendo" id="mwFg">Nintendo</a> for the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Switch" title="Nintendo Switch" id="mwFw">Nintendo Switch</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Switch_2" title="Nintendo Switch 2" id="mwGA">Nintendo Switch 2</a>. Subscribers to the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Switch_Online" title="Nintendo Switch Online" id="mwGQ">Nintendo Switch Online</a> service have access to several dedicated Nintendo Classics apps, each one containing an emulator for a previous Nintendo game console with a library of playable games. Games are accessible as long as the user has an active subscription, although users must connect to the internet at least once a week to access the apps whilst offline. The library was launched alongside the Nintendo Switch Online service in 2018 with 20 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Entertainment_System" title="Nintendo Entertainment System" id="mwGg">Nintendo Entertainment System</a> games, and has expanded to include games from several other consoles, with new games being added on an irregular basis. Subscribers to the more expensive Nintendo Switch Online subscription tier, titled "Expansion Pack",<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"group":"lower-alpha"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"},"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"efn","href":"./Template:Efn"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Full title: \"Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack\""}},"i":0}}]}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-4" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwGw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHQ">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHg">]</span></span></a></sup> have access to more consoles. The library features numerous games that were not available on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Virtual_Console" title="Virtual Console" id="mwHw">Virtual Console</a> service of Nintendo's previous systems,<sup about="#mwt29" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-5" id="mwIA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIg">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-6" id="mwJA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwJQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJg">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-7" id="mwKA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKw">]</span></span></a></sup> with some games receiving their first international release through Nintendo Classics.<sup about="#mwt38" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-8" id="mwLA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwLQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwLw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt41" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-9" id="mwMA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwMQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMg">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" data-mw='{"autoGenerated":true}' id="mwNA"/></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwNQ"><h2 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Features">Features</h2>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwNg"><a href="./File:Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwNw"><img resource="./File:Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png/250px-Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png/500px-Nintendo_Switch_N64_controller_vs_original_comparison.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="5016" data-file-height="3136" data-file-type="bitmap" height="156" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwOA"/></a><figcaption id="mwOQ">The replica <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_64_controller" title="Nintendo 64 controller" id="mwOg">Nintendo 64 controller</a> (left) does not include a functional expansion slot, but the sealed cavity houses a rumble motor to include the functionality of the original <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Rumble_Pak" title="Rumble Pak" id="mwOw">Rumble Pak</a>.</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwPA">Each Nintendo Classics console emulator is accessed from a dedicated app, with players able to select a game to play from a provided list. The emulators support control remapping and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Save_state" title="Save state" class="mw-redirect" id="mwPQ">save states</a>, with most consoles also allowing players to rewind gameplay.<sup about="#mwt44" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-10" id="mwPg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwPw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQA">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt47" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-11" id="mwQg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRA">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The Nintendo Classics emulators include online multiplayer support, allowing players to play local multiplayer games remotely with friends.<sup about="#mwt50" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-verge_n64_genesis_12-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"verge n64 genesis"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-verge_n64_genesis-12"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-verge_n64_genesis-12" id="mwRg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwRw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSA">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwSQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt53" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-13" id="mwSg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwSw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTA">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt56" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-14" id="mwTg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwTw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUA">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-15"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-15" id="mwUg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwUw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVA">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwVQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt62" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-16" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-16"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-16" id="mwVg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwVw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWA">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwWQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Some NES and SNES games also have an alternative version labeled "SP" ("Extra" in some regions) which alters the game in some way, typically unlocking additional modes, starting the player with additional items or levels, or starting the player midway through the game.<sup about="#mwt65" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-17"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-17" id="mwWg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwWw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXA">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwXQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwXg">Subscribers can purchase wireless controllers based on those of the represented systems through Nintendo's online store.<sup about="#mwt68" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-N64pad_18-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"N64pad"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-N64pad-18"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-N64pad-18" id="mwXw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwYA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYQ">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwYg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt71" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-GCpad_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"GCpad"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-GCpad-19"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-GCpad-19" id="mwYw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwZA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZQ">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwZg">]</span></span></a></sup> The controllers have additional buttons for compatibility with the Switch and Switch 2 interface, and enable special <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Easter_egg_(media)" title="Easter egg (media)" id="mwZw">Easter eggs</a> when used with the corresponding console emulator.<sup about="#mwt72" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-N64pad_18-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"N64pad"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-N64pad-18" id="mwaA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwaQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwag">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt73" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-GCpad_19-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"GCpad"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-GCpad-19" id="mwbA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbg">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt76" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-20"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-20" id="mwcA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwcQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcg">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwdg"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Nintendo_Entertainment_System">Nintendo Entertainment System</h3>
<p id="mwdw">The Nintendo Switch Online service launched on September 19, 2018, with 20 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Entertainment_System" title="Nintendo Entertainment System" id="mweA">Nintendo Entertainment System</a> (NES) games available for play at launch. During its first year, Nintendo Classics provided a new batch of NES games on a monthly basis.<sup about="#mwt85" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-21" rel="dc:references" September</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt79"> </span><span about="#mwt79">2,</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt79"> </span><span about="#mwt79">2026</span><sup class="plainlinks </section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwBUE"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Super_Nintendo_Entertainment_System">Super Nintendo Entertainment System</h3>
<p id="mwBUI">Announced in a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Direct" title="Nintendo Direct" id="mwBUM">Nintendo Direct</a> on September 4, 2019, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Super_Nintendo_Entertainment_System" title="Super Nintendo Entertainment System" id="mwBUQ">Super Nintendo Entertainment System</a> (SNES) games were added to the service worldwide with 20 titles on September 5, 2019.<sup about="#mwt543" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-snes_74-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"snes"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-snes-74"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-snes-74" id="mwBUU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBUY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUc">[</span>61<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUg">]</span></span></a></sup> An update on July 29, 2025, added the ability to remap each game's controls,<sup about="#mwt546" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-75" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-75"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-75" id="mwBUk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBUo"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUs">[</span>62<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBUw">]</span></span></a></sup> as well as support for <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Super_NES_Mouse" title="Super NES Mouse" id="mwBU0">Super NES Mouse</a> controls with compatible games; Switch 2 allows these games to be controlled with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Joy-Con_2" title="Joy-Con 2" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBU4">Joy-Con 2</a>'s mouse controls, while playing on Switch requires a compatible <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./USB_mouse" title="USB mouse" class="mw-redirect" id="mwBU8">USB mouse</a>.<sup about="#mwt549" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-76" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-76"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-76" id="mwBVA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBVE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVI">[</span>63<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVM">]</span></span></a></sup> <span about="#mwt537" typeof="mw:Transclusion" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2025"},"2":{"wt":"10"},"3":{"wt":"09"},"df":{"wt":"US"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwBVQ">As of October</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt537"> </span><span about="#mwt537">9,</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt537"> </span><span about="#mwt537">2025</span><sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;" about="#mwt537"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt537"></span><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_October_2025" about="#mwt537"/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements" about="#mwt537" id="mwBVU"/>, there are <b id="mwBVY">85</b><sup about="#mwt538" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-77" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"group":"lower-alpha"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-77"},"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"efn","href":"./Template:Efn"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"77 games in North America and PAL regions, 13 of which are exclusive to these regions; 72 games in Japan, 8 of which are exclusive to this region."}},"i":0}}]}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-77" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwBVc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwBVg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVk">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwBVo">]</span></span></a></sup> games and 7 "SP" variations available, including the following:</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwCQc"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Game_Boy_and_Game_Boy_Color">Game Boy and Game Boy Color</h3>
<p id="mwCQg">Announced in a Nintendo Direct on February 8, 2023, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Game_Boy" title="Game Boy" id="mwCQk">Game Boy</a> (GB) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Game_Boy_Color" title="Game Boy Color" id="mwCQo">Game Boy Color</a> (GBC) games were added to the service worldwide with 10 games the same day.<sup about="#mwt876" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-GBLaunch_108-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"GBLaunch"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-GBLaunch-108"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-GBLaunch-108" id="mwCQs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCQw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQ0">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCQ4">]</span></span></a></sup> The Game Boy emulator includes multiple display settings that recreate the visual appearance and color palettes of the original Game Boy, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Game_Boy_Pocket" title="Game Boy Pocket" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCQ8">Game Boy Pocket</a>, or Game Boy Color.<sup about="#mwt879" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-109" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-109"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-109" id="mwCRA"><span title="Super Game Boy" id="mwCRQ">Super Game Boy</a> features are not emulated. <span about="#mwt870" typeof="mw:Transclusion" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2026"},"2":{"wt":"10"},"3":{"wt":"27"},"df":{"wt":"US"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwCRU">As of October</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" <section data-mw-section-id="7" id="mwCzY"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Nintendo_64">Nintendo 64</h3>
<p id="mwCzc">Announced in a Nintendo Direct on September 23, 2021,<sup about="#mwt1056" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-verge_n64_genesis_12-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"verge n64 genesis"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-verge_n64_genesis-12" id="mwCzg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCzk"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzo">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCzs">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_64" title="Nintendo 64" id="mwCzw">Nintendo 64</a> (N64) games were added to the service worldwide with nine titles on October 25, 2021.<sup about="#mwt1059" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-October_2021_126-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"October 2021"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-October_2021-126"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-October_2021-126" id="mwCz0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCz4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwCz8">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0A">]</span></span></a></sup> Games are based on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./NTSC" title="NTSC" id="mwC0E">NTSC</a> releases using 60<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwC0I"> </span>Hz timing; select games also have the option to play the European versions which run at their original <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./PAL" title="PAL" id="mwC0M">PAL</a> 50<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwC0Q"> </span>Hz speed, including those that support multiple languages.<sup about="#mwt1062" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-127" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-127"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-127" id="mwC0U"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC0Y"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0c">[</span>95<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0g">]</span></span></a></sup> The app does not emulate the ability to save to a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Controller_Pak" title="Controller Pak" class="mw-redirect" id="mwC0k">Controller Pak</a>, meaning some games can only save progress through the use of save states.<sup about="#mwt1065" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-128" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-128"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-128" id="mwC0o"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC0s"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC0w">[</span>96<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC00">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1068" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-129" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-129"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-129" id="mwC04"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC08"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1A">[</span>97<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1E">]</span></span></a></sup> An update on June 5, 2025 added the ability to remap each game's control scheme.<sup about="#mwt1069" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-N64S2_130-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"N64S2"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-N64S2-130" id="mwC1I"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC1M"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1Q">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1U">]</span></span></a></sup> Players on the Nintendo Switch 2 are also able to rewind gameplay and apply a CRT filter.<sup about="#mwt1072" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-N64S2_130-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"N64S2"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-N64S2-130"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-N64S2-130" id="mwC1Y"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC1c"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1g">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwC1k">]</span></span></a></sup> Games that received a Z rating from the Japanese <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Computer_Entertainment_Rating_Organization" title="Computer Entertainment Rating Organization" id="mwC1o">CERO</a> rating board or an M rating from the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Entertainment_Software_Rating_Board" title="Entertainment Software Rating Board" id="mwC1s">ESRB</a> are available as part of a separate "18+" application in Japan or "Mature 17+" application in western regions.<sup about="#mwt1075" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-131" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-131"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-131" id="mwC1w"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwC10"><span </section><section data-mw-section-id="8" id="mwDm8"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Sega_Genesis_/_Mega_Drive"><span id="Sega_Genesis_.2F_Mega_Drive" typeof="mw:FallbackId"></span>Sega Genesis / Mega Drive</h3>
<p id="mwDnA">Announced in a Nintendo Direct on September 23, 2021, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Sega_Genesis" title="Sega Genesis" id="mwDnE">Sega Genesis</a> games were added to the service worldwide with 15 titles on October 25, 2021.<sup about="#mwt1401" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-October_2021_126-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"October 2021"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-October_2021-126" id="mwDnI"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwDnM"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnQ">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDnU">]</span></span></a></sup> It is the only third-party game system available on the service, and the only one to not carry the Nintendo Classics branding. <span about="#mwt1397" typeof="mw:Transclusion" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2025"},"2":{"wt":"04"},"3":{"wt":"11"},"df":{"wt":"US"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwDnY">As of April</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" style="display:none;" about="#mwt1397"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span </section><section data-mw-section-id="10" id="mwEd0"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="GameCube">GameCube</h3><!-- Use North American titles when applicable -->

GameCube games are only available on Nintendo Switch 2.<sup about="#mwt1710" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-GClaunch_200-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" customize controls for each game.<sup about="#mwt1713" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-201" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" href="./GameCube_controller" title="GameCube controller" id="mwEeg">GameCube controllers</a> via the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./GameCube_controller#Super_Smash_Bros._for_Wii_U_Edition_controller" </section><section data-mw-section-id="11" id="mwEp8"><h3 data-mw-wikitext="" id="Virtual_Boy">Virtual Boy</h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwEqA"><a href="./File:Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png" class="mw-file-description" id="mwEqE"><img resource="./File:Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png/250px-Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png/500px-Nintendo_Switch_Virtual_Boy_operation_demonstration.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3721" data-file-height="3525" data-file-type="bitmap" height="237" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwEqI"/></a><figcaption id="mwEqM">Main body of Virtual Boy replica in the open position, showing the removable red lenses, with an OLED Switch going into the slot, showing the two separate images of the Virtual Boy boot screen</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwEqQ">Announced in a Nintendo Direct on September 12, 2025, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Virtual_Boy" title="Virtual Boy" id="mwEqU">Virtual Boy</a> (VB) games were added to the service on February 17, 2026, with seven games available at launch.<sup about="#mwt1790" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:4_214-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":4"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-:4-214" id="mwEqY"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEqc"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEqg">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEqk">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1791" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-accessory_215-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"accessory"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-accessory-215" id="mwEqo"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEqs"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEqw">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEq0">]</span></span></a></sup> The games display two separate images on either side of the screen to recreate the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Stereoscopic_3D" title="Stereoscopic 3D" class="mw-redirect" id="mwEq4">stereoscopic 3D</a> effect of the original system.<sup about="#mwt1794" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-216" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-216"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-216" id="mwEq8"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwErA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwErE">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwErI">]</span></span></a></sup> The games cannot be displayed in full screen or played while the system is docked, and require the use of an additional headset accessory for proper play.<sup about="#mwt1795" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-accessory_215-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"accessory"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-accessory-215" id="mwErM"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwErQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwErU">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwErY">]</span></span></a></sup> The accessory is available in two formats: a plastic mount based on the original system, and a cardboard sleeve.<sup about="#mwt1798" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-accessory_215-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"accessory"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-accessory-215"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-accessory-215" id="mwErc"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwErg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwErk">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEro">]</span></span></a></sup> While not officially supported,<sup about="#mwt1801" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-217" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-217"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-217" id="mwErs"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwErw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEr0">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEr4">]</span></span></a></sup> the Virtual Boy headsets are also compatible with games that supported the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Nintendo_Labo_VR_Kit" title="Nintendo Labo VR Kit" class="mw-redirect" id="mwEr8">Nintendo Labo VR Kit</a> and vice versa.<sup about="#mwt1804" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-218" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-218"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-218" id="mwEsA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEsE"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEsI">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEsM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt1807" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-219" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-219"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-219" id="mwEsQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEsU"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEsY">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEsc">]</span></span></a></sup> Players can adjust the screen size and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Inter-pupillary_distance" title="Inter-pupillary distance" class="mw-redirect" id="mwEsg">inter-pupillary distance</a> of the display to refine the 3D effect.<sup about="#mwt1810" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-220" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-220"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-220" id="mwEsk"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEso"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEss">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEsw">]</span></span></a></sup> An update to the application on August 4, 2026, added the ability to view the games in other colors.<sup about="#mwt1811" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:5_211-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":5"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-:5-211" id="mwEs0"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEs4"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEs8">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEtA">]</span></span></a></sup> In addition to released games, the Virtual Boy library includes a pair of previously unreleased games, <i id="mwEtE"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Dragon_Hopper" title="Dragon Hopper" id="mwEtI">Dragon Hopper</a></i> and <i id="mwEtM"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="./Zero_Racers" title="Zero Racers" id="mwEtQ">Zero Racers</a></i>.<sup about="#mwt1814" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:4_214-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":4"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:4-214"}}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-:4-214" id="mwEtU"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEtY"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEtc">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEtg">]</span></span></a></sup> <span about="#mwt1786" typeof="mw:Transclusion" data-mw='{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"As of","href":"./Template:As_of"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"2026"},"2":{"wt":"8"},"3":{"wt":"4"},"df":{"wt":"US"}},"i":0}}]}' id="mwEtk">As of August</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt1786"> </span><span about="#mwt1786">4,</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt1786"> </span><span about="#mwt1786">2026</span><sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;" about="#mwt1786"><a rel="mw:ExtLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit" class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nintendo_Classics&amp;action=edit"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span>update<span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></a></sup><span typeof="mw:Nowiki" about="#mwt1786"></span><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_August_2026" about="#mwt1786"/><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements" about="#mwt1786" id="mwEto"/>, there are <b id="mwEts">17</b><sup about="#mwt1787" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-221" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw='{"name":"ref","attrs":{"group":"lower-alpha"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-221"},"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"efn","href":"./Template:Efn"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"16 games in North America and PAL regions, none of which are exclusive to these regions; 17 games in Japan, one of which is exclusive to this region."}},"i":0}}]}'><a href="./Nintendo_Classics#cite_note-221" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwEtw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEt0"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEt4">[</span>a<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEt8">]</span></span></a></sup> games
